title: FRT 48 coffee: Characteristics
metaDescription: FRT 48 coffee is a robusta coffee variety from Nestle Incorporated. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: FRT 48 coffee is a robusta coffee variety. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2009 as NSIC 2009 Cf R 13. Nestle Incorporated bred it.

heroImage.alt: Young fruit trees planted in straight rows on cleared red soil, the kind of farm where FRT 48 coffee is grown

blocks.text: The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry. Compare it with the others in our [coffee variety finder](/crop-varieties/coffee), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for tree crops](/land-preparation/fruit-tree-land-preparation).
When does it bear, and how much?

A registered tree variety is described from its mother tree, not from trial plots. Each tree gave about 1,894 grams in the records. A grafted or marcotted tree bears years sooner than one grown from seed, and its yield climbs as the tree grows.

anee.io keeps the records of each block of trees, from fertilizer to harvest, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside them.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions
rows: Took some damage but held up

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting.

The pests and diseases that hit coffee fields most often: [coffee berry borer](/pests/coffee-berry-borer), [coffee leaf rust](/diseases/coffee-leaf-rust), [anthracnose](/diseases/anthracnose), [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot), [mealybug](/pests/mealybug). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Where and when to plant FRT 48 coffee

Arabica wants cool highland air, robusta grows in the lowlands, and liberica, the barako, and excelsa are hardy in between. Pick the species for your elevation first, then a selection by yield and cup quality. A registered tree variety is a selection from one proven mother tree, and only grafted, budded or marcotted plants carry its traits. A seedling grown from its seed can turn out quite different. So buy from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, and ask which mother tree the scions came from. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Pagtatanim ng puno](/crops/pagtatanim-ng-puno).

items: Buy grafted or budded plants from an accredited nursery, with the variety name on the tag.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Plant a few trees first if the variety is new to your area, before you fill the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Where can I buy planting material of FRT 48?
items.a: Buy grafted, budded or marcotted trees from a nursery accredited by the Bureau of Plant Industry, so you get the true variety. Ask your provincial agriculture office for the nearest one.
